text: OSPF is a link-state routing protocol that uses IP protocol 89.
EIGRP uses DUAL to compute loop-free paths and keeps a feasible successor in its topology table.
By default, OSPF on a broadcast network sends hello packets every 10 seconds and uses a dead interval of 40 seconds.
BGP uses TCP port 179 to establish sessions between peers.
The administrative distance of eBGP routes is 20, while iBGP routes have an administrative distance of 200.
RIP has an administrative distance of 120 and uses hop count as its metric.
HSRP is a Cisco-proprietary first hop redundancy protocol, while VRRP is an open standard.
VRRP sends advertisements to the multicast address 224.0.0.18.
OSPF routers send hello packets to 224.0.0.5, and the DR and BDR listen on 224.0.0.6.
STP operates at Layer 2 and prevents loops by blocking redundant ports.
A router operates at layer 3 of the OSI model.
RSTP replaces the original 802.1D spanning tree and converges much faster.
IKEv2 replaces IKEv1 in most modern IPsec VPN designs.
GRE is a tunneling protocol that can carry multicast traffic, which plain IPsec cannot.
DMVPN uses GRE tunnels and NHRP to build spoke-to-spoke paths on demand.
SSH uses TCP port 22, whereas Telnet uses TCP port 23 and sends everything in clear text.
SNMP agents listen on UDP port 161 and send traps to UDP port 162.
DNS normally uses UDP port 53 but falls back to TCP for large responses.
NTP synchronizes clocks using UDP port 123.
DHCP uses UDP ports 67 and 68.
TFTP runs over UDP port 69 and has no authentication.
HTTPS uses TCP port 443, and HTTP uses TCP port 80.
RADIUS uses UDP, while TACACS+ uses TCP port 49 and encrypts the whole payload.
EIGRP has an administrative distance of 90 for internal routes and 170 for external routes.
OSPF has an administrative distance of 110.
A static route has an administrative distance of 1 by default.
Directly connected networks have an administrative distance of 0.
IS-IS is a link-state protocol that runs directly over Layer 2 rather than over IP.
BGP is a path-vector protocol and is the exterior gateway protocol of the Internet.
EIGRP is an advanced distance-vector protocol.
RIP is a distance-vector routing protocol that uses the Bellman-Ford algorithm.
OSPF uses the SPF algorithm, also known as Dijkstra.
LACP is defined in IEEE 802.3ad, and PAgP is a Cisco-proprietary alternative.
An EtherChannel uses LACP or PAgP to negotiate the bundle.
VTP advertises VLAN information over trunk links.
DTP negotiates whether a link becomes a trunk.
The native VLAN on an 802.1Q trunk is VLAN 1 by default.
PortFast lets an access port skip the listening and learning states, and BPDU Guard err-disables the port if a BPDU arrives.
The root bridge is the switch with the lowest bridge ID.
In RSTP, an alternate port provides a backup path to the root bridge.
IPv6 uses NDP instead of ARP to resolve link-layer addresses.
SLAAC lets a host build its own IPv6 address from the router advertisement prefix.
ICMP has no ports; ping uses ICMP echo request and echo reply messages.
IPsec uses ESP for encryption and AH for integrity without encryption.
ESP is IP protocol 50 and AH is IP protocol 51.
IKE uses UDP port 500, and NAT traversal moves it to UDP port 4500.
GRE is IP protocol 47.
EIGRP uses IP protocol 88 and sends updates to 224.0.0.10.
RIPv2 sends updates to 224.0.0.9 every 30 seconds.
OSPFv3 supports IPv6 and sends hellos to FF02::5.
HSRP version 2 uses the multicast address 224.0.0.102 and UDP port 1985.
GLBP load-balances across several gateways, unlike HSRP and VRRP.
A standard ACL filters only on the source address, while an extended ACL can match protocol and port.
NAT overload, also called PAT, maps many inside addresses to one outside address using port numbers.
QoS marks traffic with DSCP values in the IP header.
NETCONF uses SSH on TCP port 830, while RESTCONF uses HTTPS.
RESTCONF uses YANG data models encoded in JSON or XML.
SD-WAN controllers use OMP to distribute routes and policy to WAN Edge routers.
vSmart is the SD-WAN controller that runs OMP, vManage is the management plane, and vBond orchestrates onboarding.
EIGRP uses bandwidth and delay in its composite metric by default.
OSPF cost is the reference bandwidth divided by the interface bandwidth.
BFD detects link failures in milliseconds and can notify OSPF, EIGRP and BGP.
MPLS forwards packets on labels that LDP distributes between neighbors.
A VRF is a separate routing table instance on one router.
VXLAN extends Layer 2 segments over a Layer 3 underlay.
MP-BGP extends BGP with address families such as VPNv4.
LISP is the control-plane protocol of SD-Access.
CAPWAP carries traffic between lightweight access points and a WLC over UDP ports 5246 and 5247.
WPA3 replaces WPA2 for new wireless deployments.
802.1X uses EAP between the supplicant and the authenticator, and RADIUS between the authenticator and the server.
Unlike Telnet, SSH encrypts the session.
OSPF vs EIGRP: OSPF is open, EIGRP converges faster.
STP versus RSTP is a common exam topic.
Syslog messages are usually sent to UDP port 514.
The OSPF hello timer is 10 seconds on broadcast links and 30 seconds on NBMA links.
Some older texts state that the OSPF hello interval is 30 seconds on every link.
BGP keepalive messages are sent every 60 seconds and the hold time defaults to 180 seconds.
EIGRP hello packets go out every 5 seconds on high-speed links, with a hold time of 15 seconds.
HSRP uses a hello time of 3 seconds and a hold time of 10 seconds.
RIP update timer is 30 seconds, with an invalid timer of 180 seconds and a flush timer of 240 seconds.
LLDP is an open standard; CDP is Cisco-proprietary.
CDP runs at Layer 2, so it works even without IP addressing.
ARP maps IPv4 addresses to MAC addresses.
A switch learns MAC addresses into the MAC address table.
TLS 1.3 replaces older SSL versions for HTTPS.
DHCP snooping builds a binding table that DAI uses to validate ARP packets.
PIM builds multicast distribution trees and relies on the unicast routing table for RPF checks.
IGMP lets hosts join multicast groups on the local segment.
IPv4 uses ARP, whereas IPv6 uses NDP.
An IGP such as OSPF runs inside one autonomous system, while an EGP such as BGP runs between them.
OSPF has an administrative distance of 110 while internal EIGRP has 90.
The default administrative distance for RIP is 120.
LDP discovers neighbors on UDP port 646 and builds sessions over TCP port 646.
BFD control packets use UDP port 3784.
VXLAN uses UDP port 4789.
GRE adds 24 bytes of overhead, so the tunnel MTU is often set to 1476.
OMP runs over DTLS or TLS tunnels between WAN Edge routers and vSmart.
In SD-Access, LISP is the control plane and VXLAN is the data plane.
IS-IS uses its own Layer 2 encapsulation rather than IP protocol numbers.
TACACS+ separates authorization from authentication, unlike RADIUS.
Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) and Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) are common IGPs.
Hot Standby Router Protocol (HSRP) uses UDP port 1985.
Virtual Extensible LAN (VXLAN) is a tunneling protocol for overlay networks.
Generic Routing Encapsulation (GRE) is a tunneling protocol defined in RFC 2784.
The EIGRP AD for internal routes is 90.
iBGP routes have an AD of 200.
HTTP uses port 80/TCP and HTTPS uses port 443/TCP.
Telnet should be replaced by SSH on every management interface.
BPDU Guard is a feature that protects PortFast-enabled access ports.
A WLC uses CAPWAP to manage lightweight access points.
